posts.name: 元太 親泊
posts.cooked:
Where does the bug appear (feature/product)?

Grok Bot

Describe the Bug

In the Grok Bot desktop app, sending a chat message fails with:
Authentication error
If you are logged in, try logging out and back in.
The app UI still appears signed in (signedIn: true), but chat requests fail.
Request ID: e65c9cfa-2b6c-495a-9dff-79348f44a4ef
This looks similar to:

  • Authentication error, try logging in
    (same Authentication error text; logout/reinstall did not help)

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open Grok Bot on Windows.
  2. Confirm the app shows signed-in state.
  3. Open a bot chat and send any message (e.g. “hello”).
  4. Authentication error toast appears above the input.

Expected Behavior

If the app shows signed in, chat should work. If the session is invalid, the app should clearly ask for re-authentication (and recover after a fresh sign-in).

Screenshots / Screen Recordings

スクリーンショット 2026-09-09 105415.png1087×207 12.5 KB

Operating System

Windows 10/11

Version Information

Grok Bot: 0.44.0

For AI issues: which model did you use?

N/A (fails before a reply)

For AI issues: add Request ID with privacy disabled

Request ID: cfa9f354-144d-400f-8a81-2d1f25776b29
Earlier Request ID: e65c9cfa-2b6c-495a-9dff-79348f44a4ef

Additional Information

Already tried (no fix):

  1. Updated Grok Bot to latest (0.44.0)
  2. Sign out → Sign in again in Grok Bot
  3. Cleared browser cache/cookies for cursor.com and x.ai, then signed in again
    Checks that look healthy:
  • Direct connectivity to *.cursorvm.com succeeds
    (curl.exe --noproxy "*" -I https://test123.us10.cursorvm.com → HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found, Server: awselb/2.0)
  • DNS for test123.us10.cursorvm.com resolves
  • Local app data includes gateway-descriptor.json
  • App status shows signed in
    Notes:
  • This does not look like a “Can’t reach your computer” / network-block case.
  • Cursor IDE itself is usable; the issue is specific to Grok Bot chat auth.
  • Please check whether my account session / bot computer association needs a server-side refresh.

Does this stop you from using Cursor

No - Cursor works, but with this issue

Hi @kevinn, I’m experiencing a closely related Grok Bot authentication issue on Windows 11.

In my case, browser authentication completes and redirects back to Grok Bot, but the desktop app remains signed out. Clicking Sign In again shows:

“Cursor sign-in was not completed. Please try again.”

This has been happening for 5+ days on Grok Bot 0.44.0.

I have already reinstalled Grok Bot, cleared/renamed AppData, cleared Cursor/xAI cookies, tried incognito authentication, and restarted Windows. Nothing has changed.

I created a separate Bug Report, but it was automatically moved to Account & Billing and appears to have been hidden/unlisted, so I’m posting here because this looks like a related backend authentication/session issue.

Could you please check my Grok Bot authentication/session/machine association on the backend and reset it if appropriate?

I can provide account information privately if needed.
